newsitem.title: USA: Mallinckrodt takes on big debt in big deal.
newsitem.headline: Mallinckrodt takes on big debt in big deal.

text.p: Mallinckrodt Inc's planned $1.9 billion purchase of Nellcor Puritan Bennett Inc will saddle the financially-conservative company with unusally high debt as it works to integrate its biggest deal ever.

Although the transaction is a major step in Mallinckrodt's goal to expand in the growing healthcare market, the big debt load could cause trouble as the company immerses itself in the highly-competitive medical device business.
"The debt level does add financial risk to the integration risk," said Gary Stevenson of A.G. Edwards.

The deal, announced late Wednesday, will rocket Mallinckrodt's debt-to-capital ratio to 70 percent from its traditional 50 percent - double its current low of 35 percent. Mallinckrodt had recently used proceeds from divestitures to reduce debt.
In a conference call with analysts, Mallinckrodt officials admitted the debt was far higher than normal, but assured investors that it would be pared quickly.

"We're a financially conservative company, so any time we get to that level, it's a concern. While the level is high at 70 percent, I think we can work it down fairly expeditiously," Chief Executive Raymond Holman told Reuters in a telephone interview. He was not more specific on the timing.
The deal, unveiled earlier Thursday, will be financed by $700 million in cash and a new credit line of $1.2 billion
But debt concerns prompted Standard & Poor's to sound an alarm about the company. It placed Mallinckrodt on negative CreditWatch and said a downgrade would likely follow.
Holman said he was not surprised by the move, noting that company officials were meeting with the rating agencies on Thursday to discuss the transaction.

The proposed Nellcor acquisition marks Mallinckrodt's latest move in its effort to transform the company into a healthcare giant. In the past year, it has sold its animal health business and a flavoring joint venture in order to concentrate on healthcare.
Holman said the latest acquisition would also reduce the company's dependence on the medical imaging business, which has experienced substantial pricing pressures.
"This is not just an evolution for Mallinckrodt. It enables us to complete our transformation," he told analysts, noting that the two companies had been discussing merger plans for months.

As for future plans, Holman said he would like to expand the company's position in speciality pharmacaueticals. In addition to medical devices and medical imaging, the company makes acetaminophen and narcotic analgesics.
He also noted that the company could potentially divest its specialty chemical business in the future.
"Our commitment is to return to a conservative balance sheet position, and, if necessary, we will make divestitures to regain financial strength," Holman said.
